jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Reversible Programming for Energy Efficient Cyber-Physical Systems (MSCA Doctoral Network E-CoRe, DC12)
jobs.description:
The SDU Drone Center, part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 3-year PhD position on reversible programming languages and their use for energy efficient cyber-physical systems. The position is doctoral candidate DC12, "Energy Efficiency in Cyber-Physical Systems", in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network E-CoRe. The position is available from 1 January 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST).

 

The position is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks programme, grant agreement no. 101120187. MSCA eligibility rules apply, see the section "What we expect" below. Read more about the network at https://e-core.nws.cs.unibo.it/.

 

What we offer

E-CoRe is a European doctoral network on reversible computing. Reversible computation discards no information and therefore avoids the fundamental energy lower bound of conventional computing. The network trains a cohort of doctoral candidates who will improve and popularise reversible languages, algorithms, and architectures for energy-intensive applications. As one of the E-CoRe doctoral candidates you join a cohort at partner universities across Europe, take part in joint training schools and network events, and spend secondments at partner institutions, currently planned at the University of Bologna and the University of Manchester.

The main supervisor is Professor Ulrik Pagh Schultz, whose research spans programming languages, software engineering, robotics, and drones. You will be co-supervised by researchers from the Software Engineering section, and you will collaborate closely with the reversible computing group at the University of Copenhagen, which is also an E-CoRe partner. The position connects to other ongoing projects at the Drone Center, including WildBotics (a newly started Marie Skłodowska-Curie doctoral network) and Robotic Intercropping, and to local companies such as Spaceline.

The position addresses a programming languages question with an applied setting: how do we write software in reversible programming languages for systems where energy matters, and how much energy does this save? The setting is low-energy computations for cyber-physical systems such as perching aerial robots and IoT devices. The work belongs to the E-CoRe work package on applications and builds on the languages and tools developed elsewhere in the network. Concretely, the work includes the following:

• 
Implementing algorithms in reversible programming languages and extending these languages where the application domain requires new constructs or idioms.

• 
Integrating the resulting software into simulated cyber-physical systems, such as perching drones and IoT sensing scenarios.

• 
Estimating energy consumption through combined hardware-level and system-level analysis, using the modelling framework developed in the network.

• 
Answering the central research question of the position: how do the energy savings from reversible computation correlate with the I/O characteristics of the system?

• 
Publishing the results at international conferences and in journals in programming languages, software engineering, and cyber-physical systems.

The position may involve co-supervising related student projects. You are expected to participate in the Drone Center's project portfolio and outreach activities and in the training programme of the E-CoRe network.

 

What we expect

We expect you to hold an MSc in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field, or to complete one before the start date. The core of the work is programming languages and software. You do not need experience with drones or embedded hardware, and you do not need prior knowledge of reversible computing. You should have experience with, and an interest in, some of the following:

• 
Programming language design and implementation.

• 
Functional or declarative programming, or other work with languages beyond the mainstream.

• 
Software design and development in languages such as C, C++, Rust, Python, or Haskell.

• 
Algorithms and their analysis.

• 
Simulation, modelling, or energy estimation of computing systems.

• 
Embedded, real-time, or robotic software.

We expect you to write and speak English fluently, to work independently and with an international team, and to travel for the secondments and network events described above. We furthermore expect you to publish findings at recognised international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.

The position follows the rules of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, and you must meet all of the following conditions at the recruitment date:

• 
You do not hold a doctoral degree. Applicants who have defended a doctoral thesis but not yet been awarded the degree are not eligible.

• 
Mobility rule: you have not resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays such as holidays are disregarded, as is compulsory national service and time covered by the 1951 Refugee Convention.

• 
You are eligible regardless of nationality.

Recruitment follows the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers. The process is open, transparent, merit-based, and equitable. The position is also announced on the Euraxess portal.

 

Workplace description

The SDU Drone Center is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute at the Faculty of Engineering, located on the main SDU campus in Odense. At the center we research civilian drone technologies and their applications in agriculture, inspection, energy, healthcare, and nature conservation. We collaborate closely with companies in the robotics community around Odense and with research partners in Denmark and abroad. You will be part of an international group of PhD students, postdocs, engineers, and faculty working on autonomous systems and the software behind them.

 

Further information

For further information, please contact Professor Ulrik Pagh Schultz (ups@mmmi.sdu.dk).

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
A statement of where you have resided and carried out your main activity in the 36 months before the expected recruitment date, to document the MSCA mobility rule.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
Master's and Bachelor's degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (original and an official English translation).

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish).

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected.

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under 'Cover letter' (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under 'Resume' (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under 'Miscellaneous documents' (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file).

 

The application deadline is November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position. The position follows the MSCA Doctoral Networks funding rules. The MSCA contribution consists of a monthly living allowance of EUR 5,325.28, a monthly mobility allowance of EUR 710, and, where applicable, a monthly family allowance of EUR 660. These amounts are gross contributions to the employer. The salary paid to you is derived from these amounts after employer costs and is subject to Danish income tax and social contributions. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, this may be reflected in the salary placement within the Danish collective agreement.

The preferred start date is from 1 January 2027.

Applicants must hold a master's degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC).

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants' previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a "self-organizer".

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

This project has received funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement No 101120187.

Operations Planner Wanted for Staffing Agency

Are you highly organised, good with people, and able to keep a cool head when the phone rings and the plan suddenly changes?

We are looking for an engaged and structured Operations Planner to play a central role in the day-to-day operations of our staffing agency.

Your main responsibility will be to ensure that our clients get the right temporary employees, in the right place, at the right time. You will therefore have close contact with both clients and temporary employees and play an important role in ensuring that daily staffing requirements are met.

Your Responsibilities

• 
Planning and coordinating shifts

• 
Booking and assigning temporary employees

• 
Communicating with clients about their staffing needs

• 
Daily contact with temporary employees by phone, email, and messaging

• 
Handling sickness, cancellations, and last-minute changes

• 
Following up on attendance and staffing

• 
Maintaining shift schedules and information in our systems

• 
Ensuring a high level of service for both clients and temporary employees

• 
Continuously improving planning processes and workflows

Who Are You?

We are looking for someone who can create structure in a working environment where things can change quickly.

You work independently, take responsibility, and are not afraid to pick up the phone and find a solution. At the same time, you understand that good communication and strong relationships are essential in the staffing industry.

Experience from a staffing agency, recruitment, workforce planning, shift scheduling, customer service, transportation, logistics, or other operational planning is an advantage. However, the most important thing is that you have the right drive, flexibility, and ability to maintain an overview.

We expect you to:

• 
Be structured and good at planning

• 
Be able to manage multiple tasks at the same time

• 
Be service-minded and professional

• 
Be a strong communicator with different types of people

• 
Be able to make quick decisions and find solutions

• 
Be comfortable using IT and digital planning systems

• 
Thrive in a fast-paced environment with responsibility

We Offer

A challenging and important role in a growing staffing agency, where you will have significant influence on our daily operations.

You will become part of a team where service, collaboration, and finding quick solutions are a natural part of everyday work.

Location: Copenhagen
Working hours: 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM
Start date: As soon as possible
Salary: Based on qualifications

Would You Like to Become Our New Operations Planner?

Send your application and CV to info@manora.dk.

We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will hire once we have found the right candidate.

PLEASE NOTE: WE ONLY ACCEPT WRITTEN APPLICATIONS.

There is 1 position available.

OFFICE MANAGER WANTED FOR OUR OFFICE IN ØSTERBRO

Are you service-minded, organised, and the kind of person who keeps the office running smoothly – even when things get busy?

We are looking for a dedicated Office Manager for a permanent position at our office in Østerbro, Copenhagen.

As our Office Manager, you will be a central part of our day-to-day operations and play an important role in ensuring that the office runs professionally and efficiently.

We operate a staffing agency where the pace can be fast. Phones are ringing, candidates are coming and going, and there are always people, appointments, and tasks that need to be coordinated.

That is why we are looking for someone who thrives on responsibility, enjoys working with people, and appreciates a varied working day.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

You will be responsible for the day-to-day running of the office. Your responsibilities will include:

• Daily office administration and coordination
• Welcoming candidates, temporary workers, clients, and other visitors
• Answering phone calls and emails
• Managing calendars and coordinating meetings and interviews
• Preparing meeting rooms and office facilities
• Ordering office supplies, refreshments, and other necessities
• Handling post, parcels, and deliveries
• Liaising with suppliers and business partners
• Providing practical support with the onboarding of new employees and temporary workers
• Updating and maintaining administrative information and documents
• Planning internal events and social activities
• Handling administrative and practical ad hoc tasks

You will also be an important source of support for our consultants and management team, helping to create structure and ensure smooth day-to-day operations.

WHO ARE YOU?

Above all, we are looking for someone who takes ownership of the office and wants to make a positive difference in the workplace.

You notice what needs to be done, take initiative, and make sure tasks are followed through from start to finish.

We imagine that you:

• Are organised and have a strong sense of overview
• Are outgoing, positive, and service-minded
• Take responsibility and are comfortable working independently
• Enjoy working with people and communicate professionally
• Are able to manage several tasks at the same time
• Thrive in an environment where the day does not always go according to plan
• Have good IT skills
• Communicate confidently in Danish and preferably also in English
• Contribute positively to the atmosphere and sense of community in the office

Previous experience as an Office Manager, receptionist, administrative coordinator, PA, or office assistant is an advantage. However, your personality, way of working, and willingness to take responsibility are just as important to us.

WHAT DO WE OFFER?

You will have a permanent base at our office in Østerbro and become an important part of our internal team.

At the same time, we believe in flexibility and freedom with responsibility. Depending on your tasks and by prior agreement, there will therefore be an opportunity to work from home a few days per week. Tasks that require your physical presence will, of course, be carried out from our office in Østerbro.

With us, you can expect a working day filled with people, responsibility, and plenty of variety. There is a short path from idea to action, and you will have the opportunity to shape both your role and the way we run our office.

We offer:

• A permanent position based at our office in Østerbro
• The opportunity to work from home a few days per week
• Flexibility and freedom with responsibility
• A central role with responsibility and influence
• A varied working day
• Close collaboration with both colleagues and management
• An informal, fast-paced working environment
• Opportunities for professional and personal development

Location: Østerbro, Copenhagen / opportunity to work from home
Position: Full-time
Start date: As soon as possible / by agreement
Salary: Based on qualifications

COULD YOU BE THE PERSON WHO KEEPS OUR OFFICE RUNNING SMOOTHLY?

Please tell us a little about yourself and why you could see yourself becoming part of our team.

We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will hire once we have found the right candidate.

We look forward to hearing from you!

All Gravy is the AI-native people operating platform for hospitality and retail. 🥞

We're modernising how frontline teams work, replacing scattered tools and outdated systems with a single app that's actually built for the way people work & socialise today. Our AI Colleague gives staff instant answers & executes day-to-day tasks, freeing up managers to focus on people & customers instead of paperwork. We work with some of the most exciting brands in hospitality and retail, including Gail's, L'Osteria, Dishoom, Pizza Pilgrims, Ottolenghi, Q8 and 7-Eleven. We've grown 10x in two years and are accelerating into new markets. Our team spans a wide range of nationalities and backgrounds, united by one mission: to create better work lives for the 80% of the world that do not sit behind a desk. If you want to work in an AI-first environment, help redefine how work is done in an industry, and be part of a team that's changing an entire industry, we'd love to have you on board. 🚀

About the role

We are looking for an ambitious, sales professional who wants to build a real career in sales, not just hit a quota. We want someone who picks up the phone without hesitation and runs a sharp discovery that creates genuine value for prospects and your AEs. You'll drive smart, targeted outbound into mid-market and enterprise hospitality brands. As you grow, you'll take on full SMB cycles too, owning the deal from first touch to signing contract. This is a place where people are built into great sellers.

🎯 What You Will Do

• 
Discovery-first mindset: smart questions, active listening, clear value.

• 
Fast and fearless on the phone: first to respond, first to win.

• 
Owner mentality: structured, coachable, resilient, positive.

💎 Why All Gravy

• 
Grow fast, for real. We promote from within, move quickly, and give you real responsibility from day one.

• 
A culture that actually develops you. Honest feedback, active coaching, and the autonomy to experiment. We invest in you because your growth is our growth.

• 
Work that matters. Your work will directly impact the daily lives of millions of frontline workers.

• 
You'll work with people who've built, scaled, and won. Ex-founders, operators, all here because they want to do it again, bigger.

• 
The good stuff too. Prime office location, team lunches, Friday bars, padel tournaments, wine tastings, offsites, top-tier equipment, and a fridge that's always stocked. We work hard and celebrate harder.

🙌 Ready to roll? Curious, competitive, kind? Apply, even if you don’t tick every box. Attitude and growth mindset matter. Let’s build the future of frontline work together.

Working at

All Gravy

All Gravy: All the people stuff in one employee app - built for hospitality Hospitality is one of the largest employment sectors in Europe. It's also one of the most chaotic to operate. The average multi-site restaurant group or hotel brand manages hundreds of hourly workers across dozens of locations - none of whom sit at a desk, have a work email, or receive information through the same channel twice. The result is predictable. New starters show up on day one not knowing what to do. Training happens inconsistently, or not at all. Managers spend half their day answering the same questions on repeat. Communication happens in WhatsApp groups that the business doesn't own, can't audit, and can't control. Staff churn - already the highest of any industry, averaging 75% annually - gets worse. And operators have no way of knowing why. The tools that exist to solve this were built for office workers. They assume laptops, corporate email, and people who sit still. Hospitality doesn't work like that. All Gravy is the fix. We're a communications and learning app built specifically for multi-site hospitality operators - restaurant groups, hotel brands, contract caterers, quick-service chains. Our customers typically manage between 200 and 1,000 staff across multiple locations in the UK, Scandinavia, and Germany. The product gives operators one place to run everything people-related: Staff communications - a branded, structured feed that works like social media. Managers post to the right people by location, role, or team. Employees are notified. Everything is documented. No more WhatsApp chaos. Onboarding journeys - automated, role-specific sequences that start the moment a new hire is added to the system. They arrive on day one prepared, connected to the brand, and knowing what's expected of them. Training and learning - a full LMS designed for deskless workers, supporting both digital courses and in-person sessions, with attendance tracking, completion records, and automated reminders built in. Digital handbooks - a living, searchable library that employees access from their phone. Update once, everyone sees it instantly. No more outdated PDFs or laminated binders no one reads. AI assistant - trained on the operator's own content, not the internet. Employees get instant, accurate answers to questions about policies, procedures, and their role. Managers stop answering the same things over and over. The employee experience looks and feels like a social media app - because that's what people actually use. Adoption is high because the product meets people where they already are. The admin side is a web dashboard where operators build and manage everything centrally, with full visibility into engagement, training completion, onboarding progress, and team sentiment across every location. The problem is big. There are roughly 90 million deskless workers in Europe. Hospitality alone employs millions, with vacancy and churn rates that cost the sector billions in lost revenue every year. The tools available to operators haven't kept up with what the problem actually requires. The opportunity is clear. Operators who invest in their people's experience - making them feel informed, connected, and supported from day one - see measurably lower turnover, better training compliance, and lower management overhead. All Gravy makes that investment easy, scalable, and consistent across every location in a business. We've raised €5.8M+ to date, backed by Moonfire Ventures, Scale Capital, and a syndicate of angels including senior operators and investors from Google, Deliveroo, and Peakon. Our customers include some of the largest hospitality operators in Northern Europe. We're building the operating layer for the front-line hospitality workforce - the infrastructure that makes it possible to run a great team at scale, not just at one site, but across all of them.

jobs.occupation: Commercial Controlling and Reporting / Data analyst
jobs.description:
Centrum Personale are looking for a Commercial Controlling & Reporting Analyst to join Nordic Controlling team of 3 controllers and 1 Head of controlling. In this role, you will support commercial performance management across the Nordic region, provide business insights to management, and contribute to the ongoing transformation of our reporting.

The role is enduring for two years with possibility os extention.

You will report to and work closely with the Head of Controlling of Nordics based in Copenhagen and be a key member of the Nordic Controlling team.

Key responsibilities:

Commercial Performance Management & Reporting

• Monitor and analyze commercial performance (new business, wastages & renewals)

• Top line analysis including: premium / service revenue (risk & collection revenue)

• Support the commercial budget & forecast process with local management & Region management

• Ensure accuracy, consistency and timely commercial reporting

• Track actual performance against budgets and forecasts, identifying risks and opportunitiesBusiness Partnering

• Act as a business partner to local and regional management by providing commercial insights, challenging performance trends and supporting decision-making.

• Develop and maintain commercial KPIs and performance dashboards

• Support management with presentations and executive reporting Data analysis

• Enhance reporting processes and improve data quality

• Maintain high data quality of the reports while migrating to a new system

• Drive automation and efficiency initiatives within commercial & financial processes

Profile:

• A degree in Controlling, Finance, Reporting and/or Data Analysis.

• 3-5 years of experience in Controlling, Business Analysis, Commercial Finance or Data Analytics.

• Experience in an analytical role, particularly one involving support to internal clients is a particular merit.

• Advanced Excel skills are required. Experience with Power BI, data visualization and reporting tools would be considered a strong advantage.

• As an individual, you are detail-oriented, analytical and comfortable challenging existing procedures to drive improvements.

• Ability to work proactively and independently but also enjoy working in teams.

• Well-developed communication skills and enjoy working across functions and with diverse stakeholders.

• You will be working in an international environment characterized by change, which will require flexibility and adaptability.

• Fluency in both spoken and written professional English is essential.

Job Description

Do you find Threat Hunting, Threat Intelligence, SIEM, and EDR exciting, and do you want to be a deciding factor in IT Security in our internal as well as our customers’ environments? As a Purple Security Engineer, you will ensure operations can perform their security-related tasks based on guidelines you help define.

Responsibilities and technologies

As a Purple Security Engineer, you will be a part of Netcompany Operations and our dedicated Security team. Your work will involve defending critical infrastructure such as airports, large financial institutions, government systems, and other essential sectors. You will handle tasks ranging from identifying improvements and monitoring servers and applications to optimizing response strategies and advising colleagues.

You will be encouraged to solve technical problems creatively to find the best solutions. Open dialogue about different approaches to enhancing security is an important part of your work as a Purple Security Engineer.

You will be a trusted advisor for Netcompany’s delivery and project teams regarding how to solve security-related tasks. Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Implementing safeguards to protect critical solutions and the data infrastructure of Denmark from cyber threats.

• Engaging in proactive threat hunting to identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities.

• Developing and implementing response strategies to effectively handle security incidents.

• Responding to and following up on alerts generated by our SIEM and EDR solutions, including adjusting these to ensure precision.

About you

To succeed in this role, you:

• You hold a degree or diploma in engineering, either bachelor's, master's, or have a similar qualification level in IT.

• You are motivated by delivering optimal business and critical societal solutions.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

Employment is contingent upon your ability to obtain and maintain security clearance from the Danish Security and Intelligence Service (PET).

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

Send us your application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

Job Description

Do you find Threat Hunting, Threat Intelligence, SIEM and EDR exciting, and do you want to be a deciding factor in IT Security in our internal as well as our customer’s environments? As a Student Assistant you ensure operations can perform their security-related tasks based on guidelines you help define.

Tasks and Technologies

As a Student Assistant you will be a part of Netcompany Operations and our dedicated security team consisting of skilled and committed colleagues. You will take part in defining how Denmark’s most ambitious IT company host solutions for critical Danish infrastructure and large international customers. You will encounter everything from identifying improvements to monitoring of servers and applications, optimising detection mechanisms and response thereof, advising colleagues about alerts as well as adjusting security tools.

You will be a trusted advisor for Netcompany’s delivery and project teams regarding how to solve security-related tasks.

Your responsibilities will typically include:

• Investigating patterns and implementing alerts and visualisations in our SIEM to ensure detection of suspicious events.

• Responding to and follow up on alerts generated by our SIEM and EDR solutions, including adjusting these to ensure precision.

• Configuring integrations between our SIEM and other systems and environments, including Cloud and containers.

• Configuring and monitoring our IDS/IPS solutions.

About you

We are looking for a student who can work approximately 16 hours per week. We are flexible during exam periods, but availability is expected in the lead-up to project deadlines and other key milestones. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are in the final year of your bachelor’s degree or have started a master’s degree in engineering, computer science, software, IT, or a similar field.

• Have experience with both Windows and Linux and have knowledge with SIEM or EDR solutions.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Environmental Genomics and Pollinator Health
jobs.description:
Join a growing interdisciplinary research team developing next-generation tools for biodiversity monitoring and environmental genomics. The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a Villum Foundation funded postdoctoral position in environmental genomics, microbiome ecology and pollinator health.

Pollinator declines represent one of the most pressing challenges facing biodiversity conservation worldwide. This project investigates how freshwater habitats influence pollinator microbiomes, physiology and ecological interactions. By combining environmental genomics, microbiome science, field ecology and biodiversity monitoring, the project aims to uncover novel links between aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.

The position is located in Risø and is available from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, for a fixed-term period of 2 years.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position from 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Job description
Pollinator declines represent one of the most pressing challenges facing biodiversity conservation worldwide. While research has traditionally focused on terrestrial habitats and floral resources, freshwater ecosystems may provide critical but overlooked resources that support pollinator diversity, resilience and health.

This project investigates how freshwater habitats influence pollinator microbiomes, physiology and ecological interactions. By combining environmental genomics, microbiome science, field ecology and biodiversity monitoring, the project aims to uncover novel links between aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.

The selected candidate will lead research investigating microbial communities associated with freshwater habitats and pollinator species, with a particular focus on identifying ecological and functional connections between environmental and host-associated microbiomes.

The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with a PhD student and an international network of collaborators in ecology, envi-ronmental genomics, pollinator biology and biodiversity monitoring.

Key Responsibilities
The post doc will:

• Design and coordinate large-scale field studies across multiple seasons.
• Collect and process environmental and insect samples for DNA sequencing. 
• Analyse microbial communities associated with freshwater habi-tats and pollinators.
• Direct and support to the analysis of high-throughput sequencing datasets, including eDNA, metabarcoding and metagenomic, data.
• Integrate molecular, ecological and environmental datasets to address research questions related to biodiversity, pollinator health and nature restoration.
• Co-supervising MSc and PhD students.
• Publishing research in leading international journals.
• Participating in international collaborations and scientific conferences.
Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in ecology, molecular ecology, genomics, microbiology, bioinformatics, environmental science, or a related discipline.

We seek candidates with experience in several of the following areas:

• Pollinator or insect ecology.
• Microbial ecology.
• Environmental DNA (eDNA).
• Environmental genomics.
• Metagenomics and/or metabarcoding.
• Bioinformatics and analysis of high-throughput sequencing data.
• Statistical analysis using R and/or Python.
• Reproducible computational workflows.
• Scientific writing and publication.
• Microbiome research and host-associated microbial communities.
 
The ideal candidate will have a solid publication record relative to career stage and demonstrate the ability to work both independently and within interdisciplinary teams.

No candidate is expected to meet all criteria. Applicants with complementary backgrounds and a strong interest in expanding their expertise in insect ecology, microbiome analyses, shotgun meta-genomics, microbial functional annotation, and high-performance computing are encouraged to apply.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University is engaged in research programs and advisory work covering the major biological sub-disciplines. We conduct innovative, advanced research in the areas of aquatic biology and ecology, Arctic environments and ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation biology, and wildlife management. The Department currently employs approximately 300 academic and technical staff, as well as many PhD students.

The qualified candidate will work in a supportive and internationally engaged scientific environment at the Centre for Nature-based Solutions. The department aims to be a supportive and encourag-ing workplace that offers interesting challenges, collaborative colleagues, and avenues for academic growth. The department actively facilitates a healthy integration of work and personal life and aspires to recruit and maintain highly skilled individuals who prioritise curiosity and trust.

What we offer 
The department/centre offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment 
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance. 
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Aarhus University, Frederiksborgvej 399, DK-4000 Roskilde, Denmark, approximately 40 km west of Copenhagen.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Georgina Brennna (g.brennan@ecos.au.dk)

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 30 October 2026. 

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Do you want to work with modern tools and processes within software quality assurance? Are you passionate about building reliable software through testing and automation? Are you ready for an educational internship in an international green-tech company?

We offer more than just an internship

The applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, but you can expect a response within six weeks. Any details about the internship will be individually agreed upon. However, the internship is expected to run from the beginning of February 2027 until the end of June 2027.

Do you have a strategic and commercial mindset and do you have experience in portfolio optimization and marketing management of Consumer Healthcare brands? Then you might be our new Global Portfolio & Marketing Manager

About the job

As our Global Portfolio & Marketing Manager, Consumer Healthcare you will have two main objectives: 1) Maintain a healthy, commercially relevant and optimized Consumer Healthcare Portfolio across categories and markets, and 2) Drive and own one of our global Consumer Healthcare categories across markets in accordance with the business objectives and the commercial strategy.

The role ensures strong day-to-day portfolio management across categories and markets. This requires strong analytical skills and a solid commercial understanding combined with an ability to ensure stakeholder management along the value chain. Furthermore, the role ensures category ownership of a specified global Consumer Healthcare category (e.g., Allergy) which includes maintenance and development of the category through marketing initiatives, launch of new products, best-practice sharing across markets as well as continuous performance follow-ups.

Your key responsibilities:

• Define and drive yearly cross-country strategy plan for the given Consumer Healthcare category

• Ensure cross-country marketing initiatives and best-practice sharing to support the growth journey

• Further build the product pipeline in close collaboration with the Business Development team

• Portfolio analysis across the full Consumer Healthcare portfolio to identify optimization opportunities in accordance with the commercial strategy

• Owning and driving pruning processes in collaboration the global- and local marketing teams

• P&L responsibility for the given Consumer Healthcare category

• Manage advertising & promotion budget securing investment in projects that drive the best ROI

• Manage relationships with stakeholders across the value chain, local marketing teams as well as external stakeholders such as creative agencies

In this role you will report to Director, Global Marketing, Malene Reimers. Please note that this position is a parental cover lasting 12 months, but we expect to extend the position following the maternity cover to support our growth journey.

Who are you?

The ideal candidate brings a relevant educational background and minimum 5 years of experience from a somewhat similar position within an international consumer-focused organization, preferably in the Consumer Healthcare sector.

We are looking for a candidate with strong analytical skills, solid commercial understanding and great communication skills. You have a structured and well-organized approach and can manage complex projects effectively, while your analytical competencies enable data-driven decision-making and clear recommendations.

As a professional, you work independently and have successfully managed product portfolios and led brands or categories. Additionally, you have exceptional stakeholder management skills and experience working in a matrix organization as this role requires collaboration across diverse teams and functions.

Lastly, you must be an empathetic team player with good interpersonal skills.

Who are we?

The position sits within the Global Marketing team, and you will report to the Global Marketing Director, Consumer Healthcare. We are a small professional, and ambitious team which includes senior marketing professionals. Our culture is characterized by openness, a strong can-do-attitude and great team spirit.

Why should you join Orifarm?

At Orifarm, we are united by a shared purpose: improving access to affordable medicine for the people who need it. Founded in Odense in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We live by the mindset Challenge Accepted. It reflects our explorer spirit and can-do attitude, where challenges are perceived as opportunities. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, enabling our employees to shape their professional development. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

We invite you to join Orifarm, if you are curious, ambitious, and accept the challenge of bringing better deals of medicine to millions.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

Job location

The position can be located at our headquarters in Odense or office in Søborg.

Join Ambu’s global procurement transformation as a Project Sourcing Manager, where you will primarily drive sourcing activities in new product development (NPD) and key sourcing projects, while also contributing to category management to ensure continuity, scalability, and long-term value.

You will operate at the intersection of innovation, cost, technology, and supply risk, helping Ambu bring life-saving solutions to market with strong and competitive business cases.

This role combines hands‑on project sourcing with selected category responsibilities, offering the opportunity to influence both near‑term delivery and long‑term procurement value.

You will be based at Ambu’s HQ in Ballerup, Denmark, as part of Global Direct Procurement team, reporting directly to the Director of Direct Procurement.

**The role

**As Project Sourcing Manager you will be leading sourcing activities across NPD, sourcing and technology development projects, ensuring the right materials, technologies, and suppliers are selected to support innovation, quality, sustainability, and robust financial outcomes.

Alongside this, you will take on selected category responsibilities linked to:

• Categories where you act as sourcing lead on multiple projects

• Post‑industrialization consolidation and supplier strategy execution

• Close alignment and handover with Global Category Managers

You will collaborate closely with R&D, Quality, Global Supply Chain, Operations and Finance, acting as procurement’s commercial and sourcing point of contact throughout the product lifecycle.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Lead end‑to‑end sourcing in NPD, sourcing, and technology development projects, from early concept through ramp‑up and handover to operations.

• Drive supplier and material selection, make/buy decisions, and sourcing strategies aligned with project milestones and governance.

• Lead RFI/RFQ/RFP activities for project‑specific sourcing and negotiate commercial, contractual, and supply agreements.

• Enable early supplier involvement (ESI) to support design‑to‑cost, design‑for‑manufacturability, and innovation access.

• Own and validate procurement inputs to business cases, including cost drivers, CAPEX, lead time, and lifecycle considerations, while challenging assumptions to secure competitive solutions

• Proactively identify and mitigate supply, capacity, and technology risks, ensuring compliance with quality, regulatory, and sustainability requirements.

• Contribute to selected category initiatives by supporting supplier strategy execution, consolidation, and structured handover from project to category sourcing.

**Suggested candidate profile

****Skills

**Skills and experiences can be earned in many different ways, and we understand that the best fit for the role cannot be prescribed on paper. You are however likely to succeed in this position if you have:

• A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Procurement, Business, or similar.

• 3–5 years of experience in procurement, with strong exposure to project sourcing and/or NPD environments.

• Solid experience working in cross‑functional project teams, preferably with R&D and product development.

• Strong skills in supplier and material selection, cost modeling, negotiations, and contract execution.

• Hands‑on experience running RFI/RFQ/RFP processes, cost breakdowns, and supplier comparisons.

• Strong analytical capabilities and the ability to translate complexity into clear sourcing recommendations.

• Excellent project management, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.

• A proactive, structured, and ownership‑driven mindset with strong business focus.

• Ability to operate effectively in a dynamic, fast‑paced global environment.

• Experience in additional Direct Procurement categories is considered an advantage.

Please note: The internal job title for this role will be Strategic Procurement Manager, Direct Procurement.
